content: First-class Go support on Azure Functions Flex Consumption is now generally available. The Go worker offers a code-first programming model with typed Go handlers, standard Go modules, and integration with Azure Functions Core Tools and Azure CLI. Developers can build HTTP APIs, scheduled jobs, event-processing applications, integration workloads, and durable workflows without introducing a second application language or a custom-handler abstraction. The release supports Azure Functions triggers, typed batch processing, Blob Storage SDK client injection, and generic registration for compatible extensions. It also includes HTTP streaming, Durable Functions orchestrations and activities, structured logging, and configurable OpenTelemetry export alongside Application Insights host telemetry. Azure Functions Core Tools supports local development, packaging, and deployment. Unlike the existing custom-handler path for Go, native worker integration removes the need to operate a custom-handler HTTP server or manually author function.json files. The model supports standard net/http handlers and typed event payloads, with host-managed triggers and scaling.
